item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 6, 2026
item.description: The US dollar is trading at about ₦1,400 on the parallel market on Friday, November 6, 2026, while the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM) rate stood at approximately ₦1,348.74 per dollar at the close of the previous trading session. Data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed that the naira exchanged at ₦1,348.74 per dollar on Thursday, November 5, representing a slight depreciation from the previous session’s rate. The NFEM rate is calculated using the volume-weighted average of transactions and serves as Nigeria’s official exchange rate benchmark. Meanwhile, in the parallel market, commonly known as the black market, the dollar was quoted at approximately ₦1,400 on Friday. However, actual buying and selling rates may differ depending on the location, dealer and availability of foreign exchange. The difference between the official and parallel market rates reflects continued demand for foreign currencies outside the formal banking system. Nigerians, particularly importers, businesses, students abroad and individuals making international payments, continue to monitor movements in both markets. The exchange rates may change during the day as trading activities and demand for foreign currencies evolve. item.title: Tinubu has shown he cares about workers with ₦70,000 allowance — Oshiomhole
item.description: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” he said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, insisting that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. Oshiomhole also criticised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which Atiku Abubakar served as vice-president, alleging that it failed to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. He said the 2027 presidential election would offer Nigerians a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whom he accused of allowing multiple exchange rates that favoured people based on their connections. The senator also faulted the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, for allegedly failing to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” Oshiomhole said. item.title: IPOB demands release of detained Igbo men, alleges persecution
item.description: ….Group says release of four men after four years in DSS custody exposes alleged injustice By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has demanded the release of Igbo people it claims are being unlawfully detained across correctional facilities in the country, alleging continued persecution of Ndigbo. The group said the recent court-ordered release of four Igbo men, who were reportedly held in the custody of the Department of State Services (DSS) for almost four years, exposed what it described as systemic injustice against the people. IPOB, in a statement by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Emma Powerful, titled, “The Persecution of Biafrans Must End: A Demand for Accountability and Rule of Law,” said the release of the four men should not be mistaken for a resolution of the wider concerns over the detention of its members. The group said its legal team had identified 83 people allegedly transferred from military custody at Wawa Barracks in Kainji, Niger State, to correctional facilities in Kuje, Keffi and Suleja. It claimed that its lawyers had communicated the names of legal representatives for the detainees to the Office of the Attorney-General of the Federation. IPOB further alleged that several other people remained in detention, with some reportedly serving life sentences over cases linked to alleged membership of the group. Describing the situation as an abuse of state power, IPOB argued that political association or alleged membership of the organisation should not constitute grounds for imprisonment without proof of specific criminal offences. The group also questioned the legal basis of its proscription, arguing that the process was conducted through a civil ex parte proceeding and lacked the statutory approval required from the President under Section 2(1)(c) of the Terrorism (Prevention) Act 2013. It maintained that the signature of a Chief of Staff could not substitute for presidential approval where such approval was expressly required by law. IPOB cited the judgment in MultiChoice Nigeria Ltd v. FCCPC, involving Justice James Omotosho, to argue that statutory requirements should be applied consistently, irrespective of the parties involved. The group also referred to what it described as a subsisting inter partes ruling that IPOB was not an unlawful society, insisting that the government and prosecuting authorities should address the legal implications of the ruling. It disclosed that an appeal concerning the organisation’s status and the legality of its proscription was pending before the Supreme Court. IPOB argued that no individual should be sentenced to life imprisonment solely on the basis of alleged membership of the organisation, insisting that prosecutors must establish specific offences against each defendant. item.title: Hardship: Northerners turn to cargo trucks for cheaper journeys despite risks
item.description: By Maryam Abdul-Aziz Usman, Damaturu POTISKUM — Despite Dangote’s ban on unauthorised passengers, Northerners still board its trucks to escape rising transport fares. In July 2026, Dangote Industries Limited offered N500,000 for credible information on illegal haulage, including unauthorised passenger transport, but travellers in Potiskum say rising fares leave them with few affordable options. Baba Iyatu, a middle-aged woman, was perched atop a Dangote compressed natural gas (CNG)-powered truck, among dozens of other passengers preparing to leave Potiskum, Yobe State. Her destination was Niger State, where her daughter had just given birth. For her, the journey was about family. But with the cost of conventional transport increasingly difficult to afford, reaching her daughter meant accepting the uncertainties of travelling on a truck designed to carry goods, not passengers. Baba Iyatu and the others knew the company prohibited unauthorised passengers on its trucks. Yet they argued that those enforcing the restrictions did not understand their economic circumstances. To them, the arrangement offered cheaper travel while giving drivers and their assistants opportunities to earn extra money. Their predicament captures a troubling reality in Nigeria: when the price of moving from one place to another becomes prohibitive, some people are willing to sacrifice comfort and safety to reach their destinations. The difference in cost is stark. Lagos fare A transport union worker known as agbero (name withheld), was interviewed at the ‘Tashan Na Tsira’ Motor Park in Potiskum, and he told the Arewa Voice correspondent that a bus journey from Potiskum to Lagos, which previously cost about N15,000, now costs approximately N35,000. By comparison, passengers can negotiate rides on heavy-duty trucks for between N5,000 and N10,000, depending on the driver’s mood. The difference can amount to as much as N30,000 on a single journey. For people already struggling with the cost of food, accommodation and other necessities, that saving can determine whether a journey is possible at all. Fuel prices have compounded the problem. In September 2026, petrol prices reached around N1,400 per litre in parts of Nigeria and N1,500 in some northern locations, while diesel exceeded N2,000 per litre, according to Reuters. Rising fuel costs add to the expenses facing transport operators, who must also contend with maintenance, spare parts and other running costs. But the passengers negotiating rides at Potiskum’s ‘Baban Tasha Park’ are not all travelling for the same reasons. item.title: High Court Ruling: AA candidate warns against weakening opposition
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The presidential candidate of the Action Alliance (AA), Faduri Oluwadare Joseph, has warned that increasing judicial involvement in political party disputes could undermine democratic participation and weaken opposition politics ahead of the 2027 general elections. Joseph, popularly known as Fadojoe, expressed concern over the implications of the Federal High Court judgment concerning the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the presidential nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. In a statement issued under his Operation Rescue Nigeria 2027 platform, the AA candidate said the judgment had raised questions about the independence of the judiciary, the future of political competition and the state of Nigeria’s democracy. He said his intervention was not motivated by membership of the ADC but by the need to protect democratic participation and the right of Nigerians to freely choose their leaders. According to him, an injustice against democratic participation in one political party could eventually affect other parties and candidates. “Today, it is Atiku Abubakar and the ADC. Tomorrow, it could be Peter Obi, myself, or any other opposition candidate,” he said. Joseph maintained that although political parties and candidates must operate within the law, the judiciary should ensure that its decisions did not undermine the fundamental principles of democratic participation. He expressed concern over what he described as a growing trend of political parties spending more time in courtrooms defending their leadership structures and electoral rights than presenting their programmes to Nigerians. The AA candidate also questioned the increasing influence of internal party disputes, prolonged litigation and conflicting judicial interpretations on the electoral process. He argued that courtrooms should not become substitutes for ballot boxes, insisting that the judiciary must protect justice and public confidence in the democratic process. Joseph further raised concerns about the state of opposition politics under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, citing persistent leadership disputes, factional disagreements and legal battles involving opposition parties. He noted that the ADC had accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to weaken the opposition through legal processes, but stressed that such allegations required independent examination. The presidential candidate urged Tinubu and the APC to recognise the importance of a strong opposition in sustaining democratic governance. He recalled Tinubu’s involvement in the pro-democracy struggle against military rule, particularly the activities of the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), arguing that democratic freedoms should be protected regardless of political affiliation. item.title: Key takeaways from 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit
item.description: By Emeka Anaeto, Business Editor The 32nd edition of Nigerian Economic Summit held last week in Abuja has produced one of the most critical insights and engagements across stakeholders in Nigeria’s economy spanning across public and private sector. It also delivered some thought provoking contents on what is wrong with economic development in the country across policy strategies and execution imperatives. With significant dose of international personalities with experiences across the world, the discussions were frank and unpatronising of any vested interest. Themed, ‘‘Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity’’, the cardinal objectives were anchored on the three-and-half years of President Bola Tinubu’s massive economic reform which has already become controversial ahead of the next general elections in the country. The gathering of distinguished global leaders, senior government officials across the Federal and State levels, private sector executives, economists, and development partners were set to build consensus on practical pathways for accelerating inclusive and sustainable growth. The NES#32 actually provided platform for translating reform momentum into tangible outcomes that could expand productive employment, raise productivity and ensure shared prosperity. Furthermore, the Summit dissected Nigeria’s development priorities across five critical sub-themes, including: Work Nigeria, which entails building a job-rich and strengthening labour absorption; Produce Nigeria, which entails driving productivity, industrialization, and value creation; Invest Nigeria, which entails delivering investment, shared prosperity, welfare, and social protection; Scale Nigeria , which entails expanding growth across states, sectors, and communities; and Secure Nigeria which entails restoring safety, stability, and confidence for economic activities. The key takeaways from the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit show the outcome reinforced one overriding national imperative: ‘Nigeria must move decisively from macroeconomic stabilisation and policy reform to measurable economic prosperity, productive employment and improved living standards for its citizens’. The discussions acknowledged progress towards macroeconomic stability while emphasising that growth must translate into improved household incomes, greater business competitiveness, food security, stronger institutions and broader economic opportunities. item.title: Fani-Kayode, Seyi Tinubu, three others receive Senior Counsel rank
item.description: By Chidinma Chukwu, Abuja Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini, Chief Femi Fani-Kayode, and four other legal professionals have been conferred with the rank of Senior Counsel of Nigeria (SCN) by the Nigerian Law Society (NLS). The conferment took place at the society’s 2026 Annual General Conference, themed, “Justice for All: Non-Litigation Nigerian Law Graduates Through the Blue Silks (SCN), BOSCON and the NLS”. The other recipients are Seyi Tinubu, Olufunmilayo Osifuye, Ihudiebube Chukwumdi and Alabi Olalekan Adigun. In his acceptance speech, delivered by his Special Adviser on Media and Executive Assistant, Mrs Lizzy Okoji, Fani-Kayode called for greater protection of the rights and dignity of Nigerians, both within and outside the country. He stressed that access to justice must not be determined by an individual’s social, economic or political standing. “Justice in its truest form must never be selective. It must not be reserved for the privileged, the powerful or the politically connected. It must be accessible to all,” he said. Reflecting on his diplomatic assignment in South Africa, Fani-Kayode said the experience had reinforced his commitment to human rights, particularly in view of the challenges confronting Nigerians in the country. He recalled that his first official engagement upon arriving in South Africa was a town hall meeting with members of the Nigerian community, where he listened to their concerns and reassured them of the Federal Government’s commitment to protecting Nigerians abroad. According to him, the promotion of human rights requires courage, compassion, sacrifice and an unwavering commitment to truth. The NLS President, Ambassador Dahiru Aliyu, said the society was established to provide an organised platform for Nigerian law graduates whose professional engagements extend beyond courtroom litigation. He listed corporate administration, legal consultancy, arbitration, mediation, compliance, governance, legislative drafting and research among the professional fields covered by the society. Aliyu disclosed that the NLS was established alongside the Body of Senior Counsel of Nigeria (BOSCON), with its certificate of registration obtained on December 30, 2025. He said the initiative was established in accordance with Section 40 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which guarantees freedom of association. On the Blue Silks initiative, the NLS president said it was designed to recognise professional excellence, dedication and outstanding contributions to the legal community, while encouraging younger law graduates to embrace professional ethics and continuous development. He listed his administration’s priorities to include institutional consolidation, membership expansion, continuing professional education, financial accountability and stronger national and international partnerships. item.title: 2027 UTME: JAMB threatens substandard CBT centres, sets tough accreditation conditions
item.description: By Joseph Erunke Abuja -The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, JAMB, has moved to tighten its grip on the conduct of the 2027 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination, UTME, warning that computer-based test (CBT) centres that fail to meet its prescribed standards will be denied accreditation. The Board said only centres with adequate facilities, reliable infrastructure and the operational capacity to guarantee a credible and hitch-free examination would be approved to host candidates in the 2027 exercise. JAMB Registrar, Prof. Segun Aina, gave the indication during a meeting with the leadership of the Chief External Examiners, where preparations and readiness for the accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 UTME were reviewed. According to a post on the Board’s official X handle, yesterday, the meeting was part of efforts to strengthen examination administration and ensure strict compliance with established operational standards. The Board said the accreditation exercise would serve as a critical screening mechanism to prevent inadequately equipped centres from participating in the examination, thereby protecting candidates from avoidable disruptions and compromising examination conditions. “Only centres that meet JAMB’s standards will be accredited to host the examination. For candidates, that means a fair and secure place to sit the UTME, wherever they write it,” the Board stated. The development signals JAMB’s determination to strengthen the credibility of the UTME by ensuring that candidates, irrespective of their examination locations, have access to a secure, reliable and conducive testing environment. item.title: 2027: Ekiti PDP, SDP, APM, others unite for Tinubu
item.description: By Rotimi Ojomoyela & Omeiza Ajayi ADO-EKITI — President Bola Tinubu’s re-election campaign received a boost in Ekiti State yesterday, as governorship candidates of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, Social Democratic Party. SDP, and Allied Peoples Movement, APM, declared support for his second-term bid. The opposition politicians made their declarations at the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign rally in Ado-Ekiti, where Governor Biodun Oyebanji pledged that the state would deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, the President urged Ekiti residents to improve on the 201,495 votes secured by the APC in the state in the 2023 presidential election, when the party won in all 16 local government areas. Dignitaries at the rally included; Ondo State Governor, Dr Lucky Aiyedatiwa; Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu; Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele; and former Ekiti governors, Ayodele Fayose, Kayode Fayemi and Niyi Adebayo. Shettima said the support of opposition candidates and former governors demonstrated the growing political strength of the APC in the state. He also recalled that Oyebanji secured 85.74 per cent of the votes in the June governorship election, expressing optimism that the party could garner between 90 and 95 per cent in the presidential poll. “With a total registered vote of 1,028,000, it is our hope, prayer and aspiration that from January 16, 2027, APC will garner 90 to 95 per cent of the votes cast in Ekiti State,” Shettima said. Oyebanji promises 90% Oyebanji described the rally as a demonstration of political unity, saying the support of former opposition candidates and former governors had strengthened the APC ahead of the presidential election. He recalled that Tinubu, during his 2022 campaign, had urged Ekiti residents to vote for both him and Oyebanji, promising federal support for the state if elected. According to the governor, the President has fulfilled that promise through what he described as unprecedented federal interventions in Ekiti since its creation 30 years ago. Oyebanji pledged that the state would improve on its previous electoral performance and deliver at least 90 per cent of its votes for the President. APC targets 800,000 votes Also speaking, Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, challenged Ekiti to deliver 800,000 votes for Tinubu, representing about 90 per cent of the votes expected from the state. He said: “Out of 1,080,000 votes, and PVC collected over 900,000, this is my request, and by extension, of course, of the President to you. item.title: Terrorists abduct 10 in Ogun, demand 25m ransom
item.description: By Adeola Badru Families of 10 travellers, including a former member of the National Youth Service Corps NYSC, Olusoji Adedapo, have raised the alarm over their abduction at Ijebu Awa, a boundary community between Ogun and Oyo states, with the kidnappers demanding N25 million for their release. Although unconfirmed reports indicated that some of the passengers were serving corps members, the police said none of those abducted was a corps member. The 24-year-old Adedapo, reportedly completed his national service in Edo State last week and was travelling to Ibadan when the incident occurred on Tuesday. His cousin, Adeseye Timilehin, who disclosed this, said the family had been thrown into distress, particularly as the kidnappers had issued a 24-hour deadline for payment of the ransom. He explained that Dapo (Adedapo) had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication. Timilehin said the family learnt of the abduction shortly after 7pm on Tuesday, when one of the passengers reportedly escaped and contacted another family member. He explained that Dapo was travelling with a friend, Tunde, with whom he had served during the NYSC programme, informing that Tunde was the only passenger who managed to escape the attack and alerted the family. According to him: “On Tuesday morning, my cousin left Benin City, Edo State. He was posted to Edo State for NYSC and did his Passing-Out Ceremony last week. So, he was on his way back to Ibadan. “He was still giving us updates about his journey. At some point, he posted that there was traffic in Benin. I have the videos of the traffic jam on my phone. By the time they were able to get out of the traffic, it was already 3pm. “They kept telling the driver that it was already late and that they should return to Benin and continue the journey the following day, but the driver insisted on going. By the time they got to Ijebu at about 7pm, they were attacked by the bandits.” He noted d that Tunde told him the driver had swerved into the bush and stopped immediately after the gunmen appeared in front of the vehicle, forcing the passengers to flee for safety. “He told me that when the driver swerved into the bush and stopped, the bandits immediately jumped in front of their bus. He had to hide in the bush while the rest ran for safety and were captured. He was able to escape, but my brother and the others were taken away,” he said. Timilehin said the family subsequently established contact with Tunde, who provided further details of the incident and confirmed that police officers had arrived at the scene, rescued him and taken him to a police station, where he spent the night. He said the survivor also informed the family that a search party had been deployed into the surrounding forest that same night to locate the abducted passengers, but the operation did not yield any positive result. item.title: High Court Ruling: ADC heads to Appeal, insists Mark, Aregbesola remain party leaders
item.description: By Clifford Ndujihe, Henry Umoru, Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Omeiza Ajayi, John Alechenu & Luminous Jannamike The 2027 presidential election campaign was thrown into fresh controversy, yesterday, as a Federal High Court in Abuja sacked the Senator David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, declared its emergence illegal and nullified all actions taken by the leadership, including the nomination of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate. The judgment by Justice Peter Lifu, has triggered reactions, with the ADC vowing to challenge the decision at the Court of Appeal, Atiku alleging a calculated attempt by the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, to cripple the opposition, and other political parties warning against actions capable of undermining democratic competition. While the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr. Festus Keyamo, SAN, hailed the ruling as justice well served, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, urged the judiciary to protect democracy and ensure certainty in the electoral process. The Coalition of United Political Parties, CUPP, accused the APC of using the judiciary to foist a one-party state on Nigeria, while the Social Democratic Party, SDP, and other opposition figures expressed concern over what they described as attempts to weaken political alternatives ahead of the polls. The judgment came a day after Atiku held a campaign rally in Sokoto State, where thousands of supporters welcomed him as he began mobilising for the January 16, 2027, presidential election. Atiku, whose name had earlier been published by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, as the ADC presidential candidate, has already picked former Rivers State governor, Rotimi Amaechi, as his running mate. The ruling, however, has cast uncertainty over the party’s leadership and presidential ticket, raising fresh questions about the legal and political battles that could shape the countdown to the general election. Court upholds Gombe’s suit Justice Lifu upheld the suit by Nafiu Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman (North-East) of the ADC, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the party. Gombe had argued that following the resignation of the former National Chairman, Chief Ralph Nwosu, he was entitled to assume the party’s leadership. He consequently asked the court to nullify the actions of the Mark-led leadership and restrain Mark and Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola from parading themselves as National Chairman and National Secretary, respectively. The suit listed the ADC, INEC, Mark, Aregbesola and Nwosu as defendants. The plaintiff maintained that the emergence of the Mark-led leadership violated the party’s constitution and provisions of the Electoral Act. item.title: Kogi Senate Race :Attah urges Onoja to support Erico’s Campaign
item.description: APC stakeholders in Omala Local Government have challenged the former Deputy Governor of Kogi State, Chief Edward Onoja, to throw his weight behind the party’s Kogi East senatorial candidate, Chief Joseph Ameh Erico. A chieftain of the party, Hon. Aminu Attah, made the call on Tuesday, noting that the former deputy governor has remained lukewarm and failed to mobilize support for Erico. According to Attah, this disposition threatens both the party’s unity and the voting strength of President Bola Tinubu, insisting that the APC directive is a “top-to-bottom” campaign with no room for cherry-picking candidates. “The only way we can be sure of genuine reconciliation between Edward Onoja and Yahaya Bello is for everyone to work for the party’s victory across all candidates. The idea that we are only working for Tinubu is unacceptable and amounts to party indiscipline,” Attah fired. He alleged that Onoja’s support for President Tinubu is merely on paper, claiming the former deputy governor has refused to publicly endorse other party flagbearers. “Erico’s endorsement will not in any way affect his political fortune. We will not tolerate anti-party activities, especially now that the Ankpa/Omala/Olamaboro Federal Constituency has finally been given the opportunity to produce a senator—a position we have long labored for.” The former Senior Special Assistant (SSA) to the Kogi State Governor also tackled politicians running an “isolated-candidate” campaign for President Tinubu, asking them to return to the grassroots and sell the party across board. Attah dismissed rumors that Onoja is allegedly opposing Erico—who hails from the same Olamaboro Local Government—out of fear that the senatorial victory would scuttle his own chances of securing a federal appointment under Tinubu. “For those who think Erico’s victory will affect their political appointments, they are getting it wrong. President Tinubu will appoint individuals based on effort, commitment, and competence, not where you come from,” Attah stated. item.title: Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh
item.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has warned opposition parties against celebrating the court judgment that sacked the David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy. Ameh said the ruling should not be seen as a victory for any political camp, warning that the All Progressives Congress (APC) stood to benefit from divisions within the opposition. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday, urging opposition parties to resist attempts to turn the judgment into an opportunity for political infighting. According to him, the APC would be comfortable with any opposition party being weakened, regardless of the party’s identity or political affiliation. “The APC, which is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment, will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened. They do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said. Ameh cautioned that what might appear to be a victory for one faction today could become a tool against another political group tomorrow. “Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield,” he said. He added: “Stay alert. This is not a win for any side. It is a warning.” The NDC candidate urged opposition parties to channel their energy towards demanding free, fair and credible elections, rather than engaging in disputes over political leadership and candidacies. He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to deliver good governance to Nigerians over the past 11 years. “For 11 years, this APC government has failed to provide good governance to Nigerians. We must collectively work to bring an end to its rule. APC is the problem,” Ameh declared. The post Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UN, EU, Germany woo investors to Borno
item.description: …Zulum pledges business-friendly reforms By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The United Nations (UN), European Union (EU), German Government and other development partners are supporting efforts to attract private investment to Borno State to create jobs and help displaced families rebuild their livelihoods. At the third Borno State Private Sector Engagement and Investment Roundtable in Abuja on Thursday, representatives of the UN, EU and German Embassy pledged continued support for the state’s recovery through private sector investment. The Governor Babagana Zulum-led administration initiated the roundtable series with a meeting in Lagos, focusing on financing bankable projects and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The second edition was held in Kano, with emphasis on agriculture, livestock, fisheries and infrastructure. More than 50 prospective investors attended the Abuja roundtable. The representative of the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office in Nigeria, Thembekile Dube-Nanbe, urged development partners to translate the investment initiative into concrete action. “Let us identify viable investment opportunities, mobilise capital, establish lasting partnerships, and commit to measurable results,” Dube-Nanbe said. The EU Head of Human Development, Laila Ben Amor Mathieu, said the Union had supported Borno through its most difficult years by providing humanitarian assistance and backing stabilisation and recovery efforts. “Grants and public budgets alone will not finance recovery at the scale Borno needs. Private capital must play its part, and the role of us partners is to make that possible,” Mathieu said. She said investors could support the proposed Borno State Durable Solutions Trust Fund or pursue commercially viable projects backed by incentives, including access to land, industrial hubs and tax measures. Mathieu urged businesses to identify projects for further consideration, partner with local companies and create opportunities for women and young people. “Borno is becoming an investment story. The European Union is proud to be part of it,” she said. The Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, Dr Karen Jansen, commended Governor Zulum for restoring communities, rebuilding infrastructure and public services, and opening the state’s economy to investors. She urged investors to sustain their commitments as the economy grows, assuring the state of Germany’s continued support. “Mobilising private sector investment, including through blended finance, will be essential to complement development cooperation and support Borno’s sustainable reconstruction,” Jansen said. Governor Zulum, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Dr Babagana Mustapha Mallumbe, urged private investors to take advantage of business opportunities in the state, assuring them of government support and simpler administrative procedures. item.title: Makinde, Ajadi, Adekanmbi pledge support for beauticians
item.description: The First Lady of Oyo State, Mrs Tamunominini Makinde; the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) candidate for Oyo Central Senatorial District, Ambassador Olufemi Ajadi Oguntoyinbo; and the party’s governorship candidate, Hon. Bimbo Adekanmbi, have pledged support for the Nigerian Beauticians and Hairdressers Association (NBHA), Oyo State Chapter. They made the pledge at the association’s 2026 Hair and Body Care Exhibition and Cultural Day held on Thursday, November 5, at the Tennis Court of Lekan Salami Sports Complex, Adamasingba, Ibadan. The event, themed, “Celebrating Our Culture Through Beauty, Unity and Tradition,” brought together beauty professionals, entrepreneurs, cultural enthusiasts and other stakeholders to showcase traditional and contemporary African beauty practices and explore opportunities in the beauty industry. The Oyo State First Lady attended as Guest Speaker and Mother of the Day, while Adekanmbi was Chairman of the Day. Ajadi attended as Special Guest of Honour. Speaking at the event, Mrs Makinde highlighted the importance of preserving cultural identity, promoting unity and recognising the role of traditional beauty practices in sustaining the people’s heritage. Her participation also underscored the contributions of women-led businesses and beauty professionals to entrepreneurship and economic development in the state. Ajadi commended the association for organising an exhibition that combined cultural preservation with business development. The APM senatorial candidate pledged his support for the association alongside Adekanmbi, stressing the need to encourage small-scale entrepreneurs, particularly women and young people, through initiatives that promote economic opportunities and self-reliance. He said the beauty and personal care industry had significant potential to contribute to job creation and economic growth, urging practitioners to sustain their creativity, professionalism and commitment to preserving African cultural heritage. In her address, the NBHA Oyo State Chapter President, Chief Mrs Toyin Oladapo, described the exhibition as an opportunity to celebrate the people’s identity, traditions and heritage while promoting unity and business development among members. “Today, we celebrate more than beauty. We celebrate our identity, our culture, our traditions and the heritage that makes us who we are,” Oladapo said. She explained that traditional hairstyles, adornments, fabrics and beauty practices represented important aspects of African history and creativity. “As beauticians and hairdressers, we are not only in the business of making people beautiful; we are custodians of a rich cultural heritage that must be preserved and passed on to future generations,” she said. Oladapo thanked the First Lady for honouring the association’s invitation, describing her presence as an encouragement to women working to build businesses, create opportunities and contribute to society. item.title: Benue SEMA raises alarm over rising snakebites, treats two IDPs
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) has expressed concern over rising cases of snakebites across the state, warning that the incidents are increasingly affecting farmers, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable residents. The concern followed two recent snakebite incidents involving a 35-year-old man, Isaac Shula, and a 19-year-old girl, Mbapuun Tyoshio, both residents of Daudu 1 IDP camp in Guma Local Government Area of the state. The victims were reportedly bitten by snakes while working on their farms and have since been referred to the Benue State University Teaching Hospital (BSUTH), Makurdi, where they are receiving medical attention under the care of Benue SEMA. The agency’s Health Focal Person, Dr Amos Dzungwe, said snakebite cases had continued to increase across the state, affecting not only displaced persons but also farmers and other vulnerable populations. He said the agency had received numerous requests for medical intervention from different parts of the state, reflecting growing concern over the incidents. According to him, two snakebite patients were successfully discharged within the last two weeks, while others remained on admission and were receiving treatment. Dzungwe warned against delays in seeking medical attention, stressing that late presentation at health facilities could result in severe complications and poor health outcomes. He urged members of the public to seek immediate medical attention at appropriate health facilities whenever snakebite incidents occur. Meanwhile, Benue SEMA has urged the public to disregard what it described as misleading reports and politically motivated narratives surrounding snakebite incidents in the state, particularly those involving IDPs. The agency maintained that health emergencies and the lives of vulnerable citizens should not be subjected to political manipulation. It reaffirmed its commitment to providing timely medical assistance to snakebite victims and others affected by emergencies, irrespective of their status or location. item.title: 2027: Peter Obi Has Not Offered Any Alternative — Oshiomhole
item.description: The Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has not offered any alternative to the policies of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” Oshiomhole said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, arguing that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. item.title: ADC Court Ruling: ‘APC Afraid Of Strong Candidate Against Tinubu’ – Osunbor
item.description: A former Governor of Edo State and National Legal Adviser of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Oserheimen Osunbor, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of being jittery ahead of the January 2027 presidential election. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Osunbor said the APC did not want a strong candidate to challenge President Bola Tinubu at the polls. “I have said that repeatedly, they (APC) are afraid of any strong candidate running against President Bola Tinubu in the January presidential election,” Osunbor said. ﻿ The ADC legal adviser said the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, were continuing with their campaigns because they believed the court judgment nullifying Atiku’s candidacy would not stand. “Our presidential candidate (Atiku Abubakar) and the presidential campaign is going on, unperturbed because we believe that this judgment will not stand and cannot stand,” he said. Osunbor said the party would appeal the judgment to ensure that a higher court sets it aside. He expressed optimism that Atiku would survive the current challenge, insisting that the former Vice President had the support of the people. “Atiku will survive because the people are behind him. The force of the people will be greater than the force of those who want to enslave Nigerians,” he said. Osunbor’s comments followed Thursday’s judgment by the Federal High Court in Abuja, which sacked the David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated actions taken by the party under the leadership, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate for the 2027 election. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the process through which the Mark-led leadership assumed control of the ADC. The party has rejected the ruling and vowed to challenge it at the appellate court. item.title: Atiku Takes Presidential Campaign To Kebbi, Pledges To Restore Fuel Subsidy
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to restore fuel subsidy, improve security and create employment if elected president in 2027. Atiku made the pledge on Thursday during a campaign rally in Kebbi State, where he called on voters to support the ADC, describing it as the only party committed to addressing the three issues. “The people of Kebbi State, let me ask you a few questions. Do you want the return of subsidy? Do you want security? Do you want employment? Therefore you have no option other than the ADC. ADC is the only political party that is committed to these three objectives and more to bring about prosperity, unity and peace to the people of our country,” he said. The former Vice President and his running mate also criticised some projects being presented as achievements of the President Bola Tinubu administration, describing them as legacies of the late President Muhammadu Buhari. Supporters of the ADC gathered at the party’s secretariat in Birnin Kebbi to welcome Atiku and other party chieftains ahead of the rally. Speaking at the event, the Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Austin Akobundu, commended party faithful for what he described as their resistance to intimidation by the state government. Akobundu said the 2027 general elections would be a referendum between suffering Nigerians and the Federal Government under President Tinubu. The ADC National Chairman, in his remarks, described the party as a moving train that no amount of intimidation could stop. He called on the people of Kebbi State to vote for Atiku as president, Abubakar Malami as governor and other ADC candidates in the 2027 general elections. The rally ended with the ADC National Chairman formally presenting the party’s flag to Malami as the party’s governorship candidate for the 2027 election. Crowd at Atiku Abubakar’s presidential campaign rally in Kebbi. The campaign in Kebbi came hours after a Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the leadership of the Senator David Mark-led ADC and voided the actions taken by the party’s executives, including the process that produced Atiku as its presidential candidate. Justice Peter Lifu delivered the judgment in a suit filed by Nafiu Bala Gombe, a former National Deputy Chairman of the party, who challenged the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. Atiku rejected the ruling, describing it as an attempt to weaken his political support and frustrate his campaign. He said he would challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The ADC also rejected the decision, accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to cripple the opposition and vowing to challenge the judgment through all available judicial processes.
